correctness.rationale: The squared-error projection identity reduces this exact one-step objective to lambda_min(G^(1/2) diag(p) G^(1/2)). Symmetrization over the repeated m rows is valid by eigenvalue concavity, but the proof also eliminates asymmetric co-optimizers using bottom eigenvectors. The m-1 contrast modes have eigenvalue (1-alpha)q; the common-mode/exceptional 2x2 block has explicit smaller eigenvalue. The quadratic determinant identity det(M(r)-L0 I)=-(a-beta^2)(r-r0)^2 proves its sharp bound. The crossing r_c and maximizer r0 yield the threshold m(alpha-beta^2)=(1-alpha)beta and both displayed branches, including beta=0, the nonsingular endpoint exclusion and uniform iff beta=alpha. Fresh independent spectral calculations tested 72 feasible parameter cases and 75 asymmetric competitors per case; all matched the analytical optimum. These computations do not prove universal uniqueness: the eigenvector argument does.
residual_risks: No claim for singular beta=sqrt(a), nonsquare systems, adaptive sampling, or exact asymptotic mean-square contraction. Matrix conditioning can be severe near the excluded singular edge.

value.rationale: A natural rank-one perturbation of an equicorrelated measurement family admits a nontrivial exact sampling-law phase transition and proves when uniform sampling becomes suboptimal, sharpening an established SDP into a usable uniquely optimal formula. This is an independently useful optimal-design statement, not a generic rephrasing of the Kaczmarz bound.
residual_risks: The optimized one-step worst-case rate need not coincide with actual average multi-step error exponent or runtime.

final_claim: For the positive definite unit-row equicorrelated block plus one exceptional row (m>=2, 0<alpha<1, 0<=beta<sqrt(alpha+(1-alpha)/m)), the unique globally optimal independent Kaczmarz sampling distribution has the given two-branch q,r closed form, transition beta_c and optimum min-eigenvalue; uniform sampling is optimal iff beta=alpha. Objective is the sharp worst-direction single-step expected squared-error decrease, not the long-time MSE exponent.
limitations: Sharp uniform-in-error one-step contraction only, not an exact long-time exponent.
Nonsingular square unit-row Gram family only; beta=sqrt(a) excluded.
